fact: Namibia's MTC and Botswana's BoFiNet signed a memorandum of understanding in Gaborone providing for cooperation on cross-border fibre interconnection, IP transit and wholesale capacity, including development of the Buitepos-Ngoma corridor; the document gives no signing date, so its published date is used.
Paratus and Powertel announce that the Plumtree to Bulawayo section is live and carrying traffic, the first active Paratus fibre route into Zimbabwe, linking it to Botswana.
BoFiNet's Acting CEO says it has fibre connections to all of Botswana's neighbouring countries, including a major route through South Africa.
BoFiNet says it upgraded equipment at the internet exchange points in London and Johannesburg that handle Botswana's international internet traffic, which reached just over 100 Gbps in February 2025.
